newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends down, but off lows.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends down, but off lows.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended lower Wednesday, but off their session lows, after correcting sharply from Tuesday's strong gains which were partly inspired by a further drawdown in LME copper stocks.
"A continuation of the recent drawdown in LME copper stocks should serve to stabilize prices," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
COMEX December copper ended down 1.30 cents at 90.35 cents, after recovering from a session low at 89.00 cents.
The December/March spread ended around 1.00 cent, from 1.35 cents Tuesday.
COMEX copper stocks fell 894 short tons Tuesday to 18,826 short tons, following a 8,626 tonne drawdown in LME stocks Tuesday to 220,950 tonnes.
COMEX December copper and LME three month copper are both continuing to recover slowly from three month lows seen in early September, traders said.

Low fabricator inventories, limited scrap availability and prospects for seasonal demand strength should keep nearby futures above this year's low of 84.20 cents until there is evidence the market is shifting to a surplus supply situation, analysts said.
"Fabrication demand remains a major factor in this market helping to pull prices higher whenever technical sellers remove themselves from the market," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
Supply problems have also surfaced particularly in Asia," he said. "
But while the prompt market remains tight and the forward price curve remains backwardated, most analysts predict a global copper supply surplus next year.
